Its slope is 1, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> meet the line <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x</annotation></semantics></math>

Its tangent line is vertical, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is not differentiable at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>

Its slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-b</annotation></semantics></math>, the reflection of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> be the inverse of a differentiable function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(g(x)) = x</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiating both sides with respect to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> gives
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(g'(x)) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x) \cdot g'(x) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(g(x)) = g'(x)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = x^3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g = f^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mroot><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mroot></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = \sqrt[3]{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(x) = \frac{1}{f'(g(x))}</annotation></semantics></math> to write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(x)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{f'(x)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = x^{1/3}</annotation></semantics></math>, not at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math> itself; the inverse's derivative is its reciprocal.

items.q: The tangent function is one-to-one on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{2} < x < \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \tan x</annotation></semantics></math> there, use the inverse rule to find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(f^{-1}\right)'(1)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sec^2 1} = \cos^2 1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'</annotation></semantics></math> was read at 1. Read it at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f^{-1}(1) = \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sec^2\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>; take its reciprocal.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math> for the function in the graph, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \arctan(2x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

Square the whole inside function: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x)^2 = 4x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the slope of the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> at the origin?

mistakes.why: That is the slope of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan x</annotation></semantics></math> at 0. The inside function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> doubles it.

items.q: At which <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-values does the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> have slope 1?

The point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{\pi}{4}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is on the graph of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x) = \arctan(2x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Write the tangent line there, in the form <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \ldots</annotation></semantics></math>

mistakes.why: The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{2}{1 + 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not 2.

That slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, without the inside derivative 2.

items.q: Using the table, find the derivative of the composite function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = \arcsin(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - \frac{1}{4}}}</annotation></semantics></math> with no inside derivative. Multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(1) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

Square the inside value: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(x) = \arctan(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k'(2)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Let <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>arccos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m(x) = \arccos(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m'(4)</annotation></semantics></math>?

Why does the chain rule give no value for the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arcsin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arcsin(g(x))</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g'(3) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> is greater than 1, outside the domain of arcsine
The table gives no value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> near 3

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(3) = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{1 - [g(3)]^2} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and the formula divides by 0

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>arcsin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\arcsin(x^2)</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1 < x < 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Multiply by the derivative of the inside function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The square in the formula applies to the whole inside: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^2)^2 = x^4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \arctan(e^x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

Square the inside: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(e^x)^2 = e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which first step is most efficient for differentiating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{x^2 + 3}{\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Apply the quotient rule to the fraction as written
Apply the chain rule to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x}</annotation></semantics></math> first

Multiply the derivatives of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}</annotation></semantics></math>

Rewrite as <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{3/2} + 3x^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> and use the power rule

items.q: Find the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = x^2\sin(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That multiplies the two derivatives. The product rule adds two terms: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'g + fg'</annotation></semantics></math>.

The chain rule factor 3 from the inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3x</annotation></semantics></math> is missing in the second term.

items.q: Find the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{e^{2x}}{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > -1</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is the derivative of the top over the derivative of the bottom. A quotient needs the quotient rule.
The numerator is reversed: derivative of the top times the bottom comes first.

items.q: Find the derivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \left(xe^x\right)^3</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Multiply by the derivative of the inside function <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">xe^x</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x + xe^x</annotation></semantics></math> by the product rule.

The inside <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">xe^x</annotation></semantics></math> is a product; its derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x + xe^x</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^x</annotation></semantics></math>.

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'(e)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3x^2\ln x</annotation></semantics></math>. The product rule adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 \cdot \frac{1}{x} = x^2</annotation></semantics></math>, which is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = e</annotation></semantics></math>.

That multiplies the derivatives, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3x^2 \cdot \frac{1}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the product rule instead.
